3mpqn1.q: When the traffic light is red, vehicles must stop.
3mpqn1.why: On red, every vehicle must stop before the stop line (striscia di arresto).

7e8rh8.q: On vertical traffic lights the red light is at the top; on horizontal ones it is on the left.
7e8rh8.why: Red is always the top light on a vertical signal and the leftmost on a horizontal one.

oqz2ke.q: On a traffic light the red light may be larger than the others.
oqz2ke.why: Red may be made larger than the other lights so that it is more visible.

npztr6.q: When the traffic light is red, you must stop before the transverse stop line.
npztr6.why: On red you must stop before the transverse stop line (striscia trasversale d'arresto) and not cross it.

mvfd.q: While the red light is on, vehicles must not cross the stop line.
mvfd.why: As long as red is lit, the stop line (striscia di arresto) must not be crossed.

1vyq3bm.q: A red traffic light allows you to turn right with caution, giving way to pedestrians crossing the road.
1vyq3bm.why: Red forbids moving in every direction, including turning right, unless a specific green arrow or sign allows it.

1vunpcs.q: A red traffic light allows you to move off slowly when the yellow appears for the other vehicles.
1vunpcs.why: You may move off only when your light turns green; the other traffic's yellow gives you no permission to start.

1b07r0f.q: A red traffic light allows you to enter the junction with great caution, provided there are no other vehicles or pedestrians.
1b07r0f.why: Red means stop even if the junction looks empty and no other road users are in sight.

zwaow2.q: A red traffic light allows you to cross the junction, provided it is clear.
zwaow2.why: Crossing on red is forbidden even when the junction is clear.

gtbkdc.q: A red traffic light obliges you to hurry to clear the junction quickly.
gtbkdc.why: Red means stop, not speed up. Clearing the junction applies only to those already in it when yellow appears.

lnlxk2.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn left, giving way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
lnlxk2.why: On green you may turn left, but you must give way to oncoming vehicles.

v5mt0t.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn right.
v5mt0t.why: Green allows you to proceed in every permitted direction, including turning right.

1ms2m0v.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may go straight on.
1ms2m0v.why: Green allows you to go straight on, with care.

8at8vx.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may enter the junction only if you are certain you can clear it before the red light comes on.
8at8vx.why: Even on green, do not enter a junction unless you are sure you can clear it, so you never block it.

767f61.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may cross the junction, using caution.
767f61.why: Green permits crossing the junction, but always with caution.

ayabqd.q: When approaching a traffic light that has been green for a long time, you must continue with caution, ready to stop if the yellow light comes on before you have entered the junction.
ayabqd.why: A long-standing green may change at any moment, so proceed carefully and be ready to stop when yellow appears.

5sca2g.q: When approaching a traffic light that has been green for a long time, you must accelerate, without needing to look at the traffic light.
5sca2g.why: You must watch the light and ease off, ready to stop. Accelerating blindly is dangerous and wrong.

13xg1ry.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn left, but only when the yellow light also comes on.
13xg1ry.why: Yellow is never lit together with green. On green you may turn left, giving way to oncoming vehicles.

1hrsgnx.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, a driver turning left has priority over vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
1hrsgnx.why: A driver turning left must give way to oncoming vehicles; the green light does not give priority over them.

1txy58b.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn only if the carriageway is divided into lanes.
1txy58b.why: Green allows turning whether or not the carriageway is divided into lanes.

tqcoz0.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you must go straight on.
tqcoz0.why: Green permits you to proceed but does not force you to go straight; you may turn as well.

ywxy8j.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may go straight on, but giving way to pedestrians.
ywxy8j.why: Green gives vehicles going straight a clear run. Pedestrians take priority only over vehicles that turn.

1e2amxq.q: On the traffic lights shown, lit green arrows indicate the directions in which you may proceed.
1e2amxq.why: Lit green arrows show the directions in which you may proceed.

120hehp.q: On the traffic lights shown, lit red arrows indicate that you may not proceed in the directions shown.
120hehp.why: Lit red arrows forbid you to proceed in the directions shown.

i99i31.q: On the traffic lights shown, fixed yellow arrows lit indicate that you must clear the junction if already in it, or stop in safety.
i99i31.why: As with fixed yellow: if already in the junction, clear it; otherwise stop, provided you can do so safely.

ljhm8i.q: On the traffic light shown, lit flashing yellow arrows indicate that you should cross the junction with particular caution.
ljhm8i.why: Flashing yellow arrows tell you to proceed in that direction with particular caution.

y6swzp.q: The light signals shown are lane traffic lights.
y6swzp.why: The arrow signals shown are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia), controlling traffic in a particular direction.

12dq8b8.q: The traffic light shown concerns vehicles that must proceed in the direction of the arrow.
12dq8b8.why: An arrow signal concerns only vehicles heading in the direction of the arrow.

h4d4ar.q: The traffic light shown allows you to proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.
h4d4ar.why: A green arrow allows you to proceed only in the direction it points.

1l9mt51.q: The traffic lights shown, when switched off, allow you to pass with particular caution.
1l9mt51.why: With the lights switched off, proceed with particular caution and follow the normal priority rules.

10ii62z.q: The lane traffic lights shown, with a red arrow lit, require vehicles heading in the direction of the arrow to stop.
10ii62z.why: A red arrow requires vehicles heading in the arrow's direction to stop.

r8k4c7.q: The traffic lights shown, with a fixed yellow arrow lit, require you to clear the junction immediately if you have already entered it.
r8k4c7.why: Fixed yellow requires anyone already in the junction to clear it immediately.

boajjj.q: The light signals shown also apply to bicycles.
boajjj.why: Arrow lane signals apply to all vehicles heading that way, bicycles included.

6c4egj.q: On the traffic light shown, lit green arrows pointing upward indicate that you may proceed in all directions.
6c4egj.why: An upward green arrow allows you to go straight ahead only, not in every direction.

h7vspi.q: On the traffic light shown, lit red arrows indicate that you should proceed with caution.
h7vspi.why: A red arrow forbids proceeding in the direction shown; it does not allow passing with caution.

rpyagu.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service.
rpyagu.why: Signals for scheduled public transport use white bars, not coloured arrows.

mlnncr.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for rail vehicles (trams, trains).
mlnncr.why: These are lane signals for road vehicles; rail vehicles have their own signalling.

ccoii2.q: The light signals shown are placed at the entrance of a tunnel.
ccoii2.why: Coloured arrows are lane signals (semafori di corsia) that regulate individual lanes; they are not tunnel signals.

1nkbdua.q: The traffic lights shown are used at the approaches to movable bridges.
1nkbdua.why: Movable bridges are controlled by alternating flashing red lights, not by arrow signals.

1x15cfb.q: The traffic lights shown regulate entry onto the boarding ramp of ferry boats.
1x15cfb.why: Access to ferry ramps is signalled by flashing red lights, not arrows.

um97w5.q: The traffic lights shown regulate crossing at a level crossing.
um97w5.why: Level crossings (passaggi a livello) use alternating flashing red lights, not directional arrows.

jil363.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for reversible lanes.
jil363.why: Reversible-lane signals show a red cross and green arrow; these arrows come in red, yellow and green like standard lights.

1rfo5v5.q: The fixed yellow light comes on as soon as the green goes off.
1rfo5v5.why: Fixed yellow follows immediately after the green goes out.

17s971r.q: The fixed yellow light goes off before the red comes on.
17s971r.why: Yellow goes out just before red lights up; it is the transition between green and red.

2m9of9.q: The fixed yellow light obliges those who have already entered the junction to clear it as soon as possible.
2m9of9.why: Anyone already in the junction when yellow appears must clear it as soon as possible.

u1zse9.q: The fixed yellow light obliges you to stop before the stop line, provided you can do so without creating danger.
u1zse9.why: On yellow you must stop before the stop line if you can do so safely.

1pa8bk4.q: The fixed yellow light comes on when the green and the red are off.
1pa8bk4.why: The lights come on one at a time, so yellow is lit while green and red are off.

1da89vm.q: The fixed yellow light allows you in any case to continue and enter the junction.
1da89vm.why: Yellow does not always allow you to enter the junction; you must stop if you can do so safely.

7563ot.q: The fixed yellow light obliges the driver to go back if he has already passed the transverse stop line.
7563ot.why: Never reverse. A driver already past the stop line keeps going and clears the junction.

1hfxnd7.q: The fixed yellow light obliges us to stop in every case, without entering the junction.
1hfxnd7.why: You stop only if you can do so without danger; those already in the junction must clear it.

g4mcz1.q: The fixed yellow light comes on while the red is still on.
g4mcz1.why: Yellow follows green and precedes red; it never lights while red is still on.

56ff3l.q: The fixed yellow light goes off together with the green.
56ff3l.why: Green goes off and yellow then lights up and stays on for a short period afterwards.

xzmjuo.q: The fixed yellow light comes on together with the red.
xzmjuo.why: The lights are never lit together; yellow and red are not on at the same time.

7fcuiu.q: The flashing yellow light may be found when the others are off.
7fcuiu.why: Flashing yellow may operate alone with red and green off, for example outside regulated hours.

tlm7em.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) is a generic danger signal.
tlm7em.why: The flashing yellow light warns of generic danger.

i3vkoc.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) invites you to reduce your speed.
i3vkoc.why: It warns of a hazard and invites you to slow down.

17zyopo.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) invites you to proceed with particular caution.
17zyopo.why: The flashing yellow light tells you to proceed with particular caution.

1q5nec9.q: On a traffic light, the flashing yellow light always requires you to stop before the junction.
1q5nec9.why: Flashing yellow does not require a stop; you pass with particular caution and follow the priority rules.

1m2ddqc.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) may be placed before a movable bridge.
1m2ddqc.why: Movable bridges are signalled by flashing red lights, not yellow.

43fuio.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) may be placed before a ferry boat boarding ramp.
43fuio.why: Ferry ramps are signalled by flashing red lights, not a yellow one.

13s66p9.q: The flashing yellow light together with the red one in the figure indicates danger.
13s66p9.why: There is no combination of flashing yellow with red; flashing yellow on its own signals danger.

63xaxl.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at a railway level crossing without barriers.
63xaxl.why: Alternating flashing red lights require a stop at level crossings, including those without barriers.

f2lv2i.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at a railway level crossing with half-barriers.
f2lv2i.why: A stop is also required at level crossings with half-barriers (semibarriere).

9qmqzn.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a ferry boat boarding ramp.
9qmqzn.why: Flashing red lights require a stop at the access to a ferry boarding ramp.

1yxmyr5.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a movable bridge.
1yxmyr5.why: Flashing red lights require a stop at the access to a movable bridge.

vo8nmo.q: The flashing red lights shown require you not to cross the transverse stop line.
vo8nmo.why: Flashing red lights require you to stop before the transverse stop line.

xqpwrn.q: The flashing red lights shown are located near a police checkpoint.
xqpwrn.why: They are used at level crossings, movable bridges and ferry ramps, not at police checkpoints.

1olhz2a.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a narrow bridge.
1olhz2a.why: A narrow bridge is dealt with by warning and priority signs, not flashing red lights.

1nlmz10.q: The flashing red lights shown indicate the mandatory exit from the motorway.
1nlmz10.why: Flashing red lights require a stop; they do not indicate a motorway exit.

59wnll.q: The flashing red lights shown are located 150 metres before a State border.
59wnll.why: They do not mark State borders; they are used at level crossings, movable bridges and ferry ramps.

w08rdb.q: The flashing red lights shown indicate that the green light is about to come on.
w08rdb.why: Flashing red lights mean stop until they go off; they do not announce a green light.

1pi121f.q: The traffic light shown may have the horizontal white light on.
1pi121f.why: The horizontal white bar can be lit on this public-transport signal.

155qcj.q: The traffic light shown may have the vertical white light on.
155qcj.why: The vertical white bar can be lit on this public-transport signal.

1btbi6e.q: The light signal shown indicates a traffic light for public transport vehicles.
1btbi6e.why: This is the signal reserved for public transport vehicles in scheduled service.

cb5jsr.q: The traffic light shown applies to vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service.
cb5jsr.why: The white-bar signal applies to vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service (servizio di linea).

1iv1v7g.q: The traffic light shown requires vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service to stop when the white bar at the top is lit.
1iv1v7g.why: The horizontal white bar at the top equals red and requires a stop.

huurgk.q: The traffic light shown allows public passenger transport vehicles to proceed when the white bar at the bottom is lit.
huurgk.why: The vertical white bar at the bottom equals green and allows vehicles to proceed.

kfuvwh.q: The traffic light shown is a pedestrian traffic light.
kfuvwh.why: Pedestrian signals show a human figure; this one has white bars for public transport.

47z3l8.q: The traffic light shown announces roadworks.
47z3l8.why: The white bars and yellow triangle do not announce roadworks; they regulate public transport vehicles.

xbjmkt.q: The traffic light shown indicates possible tram track switches.
xbjmkt.why: It does not concern tram track switches; it regulates scheduled public transport vehicles.

1hhc9ji.q: The traffic light shown requires motorcycles to slow down when the yellow triangle is lit.
1hhc9ji.why: The signal does not concern motorcycles, only vehicles in scheduled service.

r19avr.q: The traffic light shown applies to vehicles with military plates.
r19avr.why: It does not apply to vehicles with military plates, but to public transport vehicles in scheduled service.

sxqqny.q: The traffic light shown is valid only for vehicles running on rails (trams, trains).
sxqqny.why: It applies to scheduled public transport vehicles using the road, not only to rail vehicles.

10yuo14.q: The traffic light shown regulates the passage of pedestrians.
10yuo14.why: It does not regulate pedestrians, who have their own signals showing a human figure.
